judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: 'previous slider' arrow button of the partner-brand carousel. Its class includes slick-disabled: the carousel is at its first slide, so react-slick removes the click handler. Its icon is #e0e0e0 from the CSS, against #ffffff (1.32:1), while the active 'next slider' arrow is #191927 (17.36:1). The screenshot also shows the left arrow lighter than the right. The measured facts in the claim are true of the snapshot. But the light grey is the inactive state, and 1.4.11 does not apply to inactive components (Understanding 1.4.11: visible but not currently operable, not required to meet contrast). So the element does not fail 1.4.11. That the button stays focusable with no disabled or aria-disabled state is a possible 4.1.2 issue, not a 1.4.11 one. The arrows are script-rendered, and at load users get the same first-slide state, so there is no capture difference. The rule ignored the inactive exemption.
